name: Nino Connector
author: ninoapp

sections.description:
Nino writes SEO articles for your business. This plugin lets Nino put them on your WordPress site:

  • creates each article as a draft first, then publishes it
  • writes the SEO title, meta description and focus keyword for Yoast SEO and Rank Math
  • uploads the article image to your media library
  • works when a security plugin (for example Wordfence) switches off Application Passwords, when your server removes the Authorization header, or when the REST API is closed to visitors

How the connection works:

  1. Activate the plugin and open Settings → Nino.
  2. Click “Create connection code” and paste the code into Nino.
  3. Nino sends signed requests to your site. Each request is checked (signature, time, one-time number) before anything happens.

Nino can only do what the WordPress user who created the code is allowed to do.

Nino (https://seo.trynino.com) is a subscription service that plans and writes the articles. You need a Nino account to use this plugin. The plugin itself is free, and every feature in it works without limits.

Privacy and stored data

  • The plugin makes NO outbound connections. It never calls Nino or anyone else; it only answers signed requests sent to your site.
  • The plugin stores one secret key in the option ninoc_credential (not autoloaded). The secret must be stored in readable form because the plugin uses it to check each request’s signature (HMAC-SHA256). Anyone who can read your database can read it, like your other WordPress keys. Create a new code or click “Disconnect” to make the old secret useless.
  • The connection code is shown once, right after you create it, and is never saved anywhere else.
  • The table {prefix}ninoc_ops holds short-lived one-time numbers and locks (no personal data).
  • Uninstalling removes the option and the table. Your posts and images stay.

External services

This plugin connects your site to the Nino service (https://seo.trynino.com), operated by Nino. Nino is needed for the plugin to do anything: it writes the articles and sends them to your site.

The plugin itself never opens a connection to Nino or any other server. Instead, after you create a connection code and paste it into Nino, Nino sends signed requests to your site (to the REST route /wp-json/nino/v1/rpc, or to /?ninoc_rpc=1 when the REST API is closed), and the plugin answers them.

What is exchanged, and when:

  • When you connect, and before each publish: your site sends Nino its WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, your home address, the permalink setting, which SEO plugin is active (Yoast SEO or Rank Math), whether WooCommerce is active, the connected user’s ID, display name and permissions (edit, publish, upload, unfiltered HTML), and your post categories (ID, name, slug).
  • When Nino publishes or updates an article: Nino sends the title, text, excerpt, address (slug), categories, featured image and its alt text, and the SEO title, meta description and focus keyword. Your site answers with the post ID, address and status.
  • When Nino suggests internal links: your site sends the titles and addresses of public posts, pages and WooCommerce products the connected user may read. Password-protected and private content is never included.
  • When Nino checks an article it published: your site tells Nino whether the post still exists, is in the trash, or is live.
  • When you click “Disconnect” or create a new code: the old code stops working at once.

No data about your visitors is sent. No data is sent unless you create a connection code and paste it into Nino.

  • Nino terms of service: https://seo.trynino.com/pages/terms.html
  • Nino privacy policy: https://seo.trynino.com/pages/seo-privacy.html
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Nino Connector”, then install and activate it. Or upload the nino-connector folder to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it under Plugins.
  2. Open Settings → Nino and click “Create connection code”.
  3. In Nino’s WordPress set-up, paste the code into the “Connection code” field and connect.
sections.faq:
Do I need Application Passwords?

No. The plugin signs requests with its own key.

What happens if I lose the code?

Create a new one under Settings → Nino. The old code stops working.

Do I need a Nino account?

Yes. Nino (https://seo.trynino.com) is a subscription service that plans and writes the articles. The plugin itself is free and has no paid features.

Does the plugin contact other servers?

No. It only answers signed requests that Nino sends to your site. See “External services” for what is exchanged.

Which user does Nino publish as?

As the WordPress user who created the connection code. Nino can only do what that user is allowed to do.

How do I disconnect Nino?

Open Settings → Nino and click “Disconnect”. The code stops working at once. Deactivating the plugin also stops all requests.
sections.changelog:
0.10.13

  • Fix: “Create connection code” no longer shows a critical error on sites without MySQL (WordPress Playground, WordPress Studio, SQLite). The site lock falls back to the plugin’s own table there; MySQL sites are unchanged.
  • The code screen now names the field in Nino: “Connection code”.
  • New “Settings” link next to “Deactivate” in the Plugins list.
  • Uninstall on a multisite network now cleans up every site.

0.10.12

  • Removed bundled translations; translations come from translate.wordpress.org.

0.10.11

  • Improvement: when Nino asks about a post it can no longer use, the plugin now says why — deleted for good, in the trash, or not a Nino post. Nino marks an article as deleted on your site only when the post is really gone; a post in the trash can still be restored.

0.10.10

  • Fix: an error while Nino builds its answer no longer takes a finished, live post offline.
  • Fix: if the site owner takes a post offline at the very moment Nino publishes it, a retry no longer puts it back online.
  • Security: a new connection code that Nino never used stops working after 24 hours. Create a new one under Settings → Nino. A site that is already connected stays connected after the update.
  • Fix: if a publish is cut off before the post goes live, a retry after about 12 minutes publishes it — unless the post was changed in the meantime.

Older versions: see changelog.txt in the plugin folder.

short_description: Lets Nino publish your SEO articles as drafts and posts, with Yoast or Rank Math meta, even when Application Passwords are switched off.
